title: Backend Readiness Continuation
request: Continue the existing backend readiness tracker from the prior phase. Add dependency-aware deployment readiness without replacing the small in-memory API: services may declare requiredEnv and dependency IDs, ready services must have healthy status, satisfied required env vars, and ready dependencies, and summarizeReadiness must surface ready, blocked, missing-env, unhealthy, deploymentStatus, and nextAction fields.
context: Phase 1 already delivered an in-memory readiness tracker with add, mark healthy/unhealthy, list, and summary behavior. The prior handoff is in docs/phase-1-readiness.md.
Required env vars should be checked against the injectable env object passed to createReadinessTracker; do not read process.env directly inside tests.
A service is ready only when it is healthy, all requiredEnv names are present in env, and every declared dependency is also ready.

blockedCount should count healthy services that are not ready because of missing env or an unready dependency chain. unhealthyCount should count unhealthy services separately. nextAction should prioritize set_missing_env, then repair_unhealthy, then unblock_dependencies, then deploy.
Do not add HTTP routing, persistence, Docker, or dependencies. Keep structured validation errors and the injectable now() clock.
successCriteria: Existing readiness tests continue to pass.
addService accepts optional requiredEnv and dependencies arrays.
Unknown dependencies and invalid env names throw structured validation errors.
listReadyServices returns only services that are healthy, env-satisfied, and dependency-ready.
summarizeReadiness adds readyCount, blockedCount, missingEnvCount, unhealthyCount, deploymentStatus, and nextAction.
